# PiHRMS UI page inventory

Checkpoint 1 inventories the checkout at Horilla HR 2.4.0 on branch `2.0` and commit `6c15617b8297b7a6775daa6c29aefcc48b1eb29f`. This is a static source inventory. It includes checked-in variants and declared alternate and conditional routes. Django, host overrides, browser behavior, and database configuration were outside runtime verification.

## Reading the inventory

- A route row represents a literal endpoint declaration at an expanded mount, including duplicate declarations, aliases, and conditional and opt-in paths. The two API mounts are counted separately because they publish different paths. Route factories and external mounts are listed independently. Paths with regular-expression syntax retain the expression where relevant.
- A unique page is a source-backed full document or inherited layout with an identified handler. Routes with the same handler, template outputs and explicit view arguments share a page ID. Context-dependent pages whose template cannot be resolved statically stay in the route index. Fragments, standalone dialogs, redirects, JSON, and ordinary exports have their own route categories.
- A shared component is a checked-in fragment or reusable layout included by at least two different logical template names. The number is a reproducible lower bound. Dynamic includes, inheritance, widget injection, and inline components can add reuse.
- Look up the page table's route IDs in the route index for exact URL names, access evidence, callable, and source condition. The template catalogue records one row per physical file. Access evidence records explicit guards and visible predicates. Effective inherited access, company scope, object rules, and middleware require runtime or individual flow review. Missing access evidence makes no claim about public visibility.
- Statically selected means the first local candidate in the configured loader order with default apps, assuming a database miss. A source reference signals use by a view or parent template, and may describe an optional branch. An unlinked file remains catalogued because dynamically selected fragments, Django admin, model renderers, and overrides can still use it.
- Checkpoint 1 designs the system. Every page and template remains **Not started** for UI implementation, and runtime verification is **Not executed**.

## Runtime precedence and redesign boundaries

1. The cached template loader first attempts an active, scheduled host/site and language-aware database match, then a global match. These records can supersede the theme or app file. The inventory determines disk order for every duplicate key. How many database overrides apply to any real request remains unknown.
2. Disk lookup searches `horilla_theme/templates`, followed by the configured app directories in order and the root `templates` fallback. Optional app directories affect the outcome only when enabled. A nested file named `dashboard/dashboard.html` resolves a different key from `dashboard.html`.
3. The main dashboard at `/dashboard/` uses the logical key `dashboard.html` and the role resolver in `base/dashboard_roles.py`. Employee self-service at `/my-dashboard/` requires an employee link. The explicitly requested analytics view, scoped KPI endpoints, and the permission-filtered menu stay separate contracts.
4. Authenticated theme values come from `get_company`, which resolves the selected company theme or falls back to the default. Sign-in uses `get_def_theme`. Dark mode is session-controlled. Company palette selection and logo precedence are independent of template lookup.
5. Central shell and shared components are good starting points for scoped, additive styles. Check the selected `index.html`, `generic/` fragments, header, sidebar, modal hosts, and both whole-page and HTMX responses. Public candidate and onboarding layouts, auth, Django admin, legacy root layouts, emails, and PDFs require separate review.

Open runtime questions include which overrides exist, which conditional routes are enabled, how tenant data affects default views, and which commands render XHR fragments versus complete documents. The source route rows can repeat a path, and first-match behavior must be checked in the running resolver. Django-provided admin, auth, and i18n mounts and generated per-record/admin URLs require an installed runtime to enumerate exhaustively.

`DynamicView` references `dynamic.html`, a logical key with no checked-in candidate in the indexed template roots. The view and its callers should be checked against the active configuration before styling the associated field workflow. The documented database override count remains unknown. [View source](../horilla_views/views.py#L1135)

### Dashboard roles and access

| Audience | Source-backed entry and checks |
| --- | --- |
| Employee | The default employee home redirects to `ess-dashboard` at `/my-dashboard/`. The ESS view requires an account linked to an employee record. Its attendance, payslip and leave widgets use their existing scoped endpoints. |
| Reporting manager | The analytics dashboard is eligible if the user is a reporting manager and does not resolve to HR or leadership. Manager visibility and approval actions use their own request and object checks. |
| HR | The home role uses both `employee.view_employee` and `leave.view_leaverequest`. The dashboard preset includes recruitment and turnover chart slots subject to the current widget and endpoint permissions. |
| Leadership and administrators | Leadership resolves for staff or superusers, or for the employee, leave and recruitment view permission combination. The role sets the chart preset. Admin routes, API authorization and company scoping remain separate controls. |
| Candidate and incoming employee | Public careers and application layouts, candidate-session checks, and token-based onboarding are outside the authenticated staff shell. Their permissions and visual states are indexed under recruitment and onboarding. |

Use the view and endpoint guards in the route table when reviewing actual access. Role classification and chart defaults live in [the dashboard role resolver](../base/dashboard_roles.py#L65).

## Priority and protected workflows


| Priority | Workstream | Acceptance evidence to collect later |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | Shared shell, navigation, company switcher, mobile drawer, check-in/out placement | Same role-visible routes and access predicates, touch and keyboard access, stable single attendance host and modal targets. |
| P1 | Authentication, dashboards, attendance, leave approvals, payroll and permissions | Same role redirects, field names, routes and CSRF. Compare desktop/mobile actions and permission cases. Trace payroll totals and exports through unchanged handlers. |
| P2 | Employee directory/profile, lifecycle, assets, helpdesk, performance, projects, and reports | Compare list/card/kanban navigation, sort, pagination and filters, modal focus, import/export, and empty states. |
| P3 | Optional add-ons, legacy fallback, Django admin, standalone output surfaces | Confirm actual enablement or alternate selection. Preserve emails and printable/PDF output behavior. |

The attendance header includes `attendance/components/in_out_component.html`. Both variants gate the clock control by attendance settings and company context. Preserve `clock-in`, `clock-out`, `#attendance-activity-container`, HTMX swap attributes, timer nodes, and the optional geolocation action and its existing error path. Keep the interactive clock in the header at every size. Test single submits, live updates, denied permission, company scope, and focus on the swapped control in a permitted test environment.
